I am working on a Lean 4 formalization involving SU(3).I define:```leanabbrev SU3 := Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ
I have a mechanical proof of the Lie-algebra-level simplicity statement for my su(3) model. The group-level statement I still need is:

∀ (H : Subgroup SU3),  H.Normal →  IsConnected (H : Set SU3) →  H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤
Mathematically, this should follow from the standard relationship between connected normal Lie subgroups and Lie ideals of the Lie algebra.

Right now I have marked this as a named axiom, because I do not want to hide the gap behind sorry.

My question:

Does Mathlib currently have the API needed to prove this for Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ? If so, what is the recommended route? If not, what infrastructure would need to be added first?

I don't know this part of the library well but my first question would be: do we even have a manifold structure on Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ? It would not surprise me if the answer were "no" and so that would be the place to start if you wanted to use this proof. I think the last time this sort of thing came up the state of the art was that we couldn't put a manifold structure on the subset of an algebraic variety defined by a smooth polynomial equation because we were missing either the inverse or the implicit function theorem.
We're still missing it because of the regular value theorem iirc

/-- Bridge theorem: The exponential of any element of su3LieSubalgebra
lies in SU3. -/
theorem exp_mem_SU3_of_mem_su3LieSubalgebra (X : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)
(hX : X ∈ su3LieSubalgebra) :
NormedSpace.exp X ∈ SU3 := by
rw [show (SU3 : Submonoid _) = Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ from rfl,
Matrix.mem_specialUnitaryGroup_iff]
refine ⟨?_, det_exp_eq_one_of_su3 X hX⟩
exact exp_mem_unitaryGroup_of_skew X ((mem_su3LieSubalgebra_iff X).mp hX).1

end SU3ExponentialMap
